paragraphs.text: Saved time is not the work.

at NN/g surveyed 521 UX practitioners about AI. Almost everyone has access, and most tasks get faster. But the average sentiment was 3.57 out of 5, and most of the written comments were negative. The telling detail: people use it most for desk work and least for work with actual users.
went after the empty box problem. His site now answers before anyone asks, because the hard part of an AI product is knowing what it can even do. A faster draft doesn’t solve that.

made a point engineers already know and designers should borrow. Software is slow because of design, not the language. Most of the wait is the database, the disk, or another service. Our process works the same way: a faster tool doesn’t fix a slow decision.
If AI buys you an afternoon back, spend it with a user.
